ISONIAZID (INH) OVERDOSE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
GENERAL APPROACH 
Consider INH toxicity in all refractory seizures, especially if on TB Rx/prophylaxis 
 
•
Clinical features: Depletes Vit B6, causing decreased GABA – seizures, lactic acidosis  
•
ECG Features: No specific features, sinus tachycardia 
•
Bloodgas: HAGMA, severe lactic acidosis 
 
•
Triage to RESUS AREA, even if patient initially appears well  
•
Terminate seizures with Benzodiazepines (high doses may be required).  
See Status Epilepticus protocol, but avoid anti-epileptic agents.  
•
Rapid ABC assessment, 2 IV lines, monitors, HGT, VBG, urine ßHCG, ECG 
•
Early airway management – will require intubation prior to Pyridoxine administration 
•
Correct abnormal electrolytes, consider other causes of seizures 
•
Crystalloid fluid bolus 20mg/kg if hypotensive 
•
Comprehensive history and exam, including: 
§
Amount and time of ingestion, co-ingestants 
§
Comorbidities, chronic medications, symptoms prior to arrival 
•
Document specific features of toxicity 
•
Further investigations: FBC, U&E, LFT, Paracetamol/Salicylate level, urine tox screen, 
imaging as clinically indicated 
SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT 
 
*Enhanced elimination  
  Consider activated charcoal 50g via NGT once airway is secured, IF INGESTION < 1 HOUR  AGO   
  Dialysis too slow, not indicated. 
*Haemodynamic support 
  Fluid bolus/inotropes prn. Consider co-ingestants if persistent hypotension 
*Airway support 
  Profound CNS depression and prolonged seizures usually require intubation 
*Specific antidote therapy: Pyridoxine (see box) 
DISPOSITION 
 
•
GIT referral 
•
Will likely require ICU/High care 
•
Continue serial ECG and VBG monitoring in ED 
PYRIDOXINE THERAPY 
 
•
KNOWN AMOUNT INGESTED  
§
1g Pyridoxine for each gram of INH ingested, 
max 5g total or 70mg/kg in children. 
•
UNKNOWN AMOUNT INGESTED 
§
Give 5g total 
§
Repeat after 10 - 20 minutes if no response 
•
Pyridoxine is available in 25mg tablets 
•
Crush tablets and administer via NGT once airway is 
protected 
•
Call pharmacy early to request enough stock, as it is 
unlikely to be available in ED 
•
Therapeutic endpoint: seizure termination, 
resolution of lactic acidosis 
 
5g = 200 tablets 
Dr du Plessis / Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
